body:
Reviewed head `021da4c` against issue #489's acceptance criteria and the existing runtime/binding/dynamic-writer contracts.

The import, version-index remapping, archive-before-`libgcc_s` precedence, as-needed retention, and snapshot serialization are consistent in the cases covered by the new tests. I found two remaining acceptance/correctness issues, called out inline.

**Acceptance / merge gate:** #489 expressly requires a 9700X comparison with #483, including the no-`libgcc_s`-import path. This PR only supplies VM measurements; the 9700X workflow is not the requested before/after comparison until that evidence is produced and linked. Also, the description begins `Closes #489`, which GitHub will treat as an automatic issue-closing keyword on merge even though the performance gate and the direct-writer split-stack PIE are still outstanding. Please either finish and attach the acceptance evidence and resolve the PIE gap, or change the closing keyword to `Refs #489` and track the unfinished writer work in a dedicated issue before merging.

I have not run the test binaries locally; this is a source/diff and GitHub-check review.

Re-reviewed head `61a68a1` after the previous findings.

**Prior review resolution:** The no-`libgcc_s.so.1` fallback tests are now conditional and assert the refusal paths. The direct-writer split-stack PIE gap is tracked in #515 rather than incorrectly claimed complete here; the PR uses `Refs #489`. Those responses address both earlier review threads.

**New finding:** The inline comment below identifies a separate `--as-needed` correctness gap for strong undefined references originating in an already-needed named shared library. GNU ld explicitly counts such references when the library is not already in that DSO's own `DT_NEEDED` list ([linker documentation](https://sourceware.org/binutils/docs/ld/Options.html)). The current scan only counts `Bind.imports`, not `RuntimeLibraries.references`. A targeted `-lhelper` fixture and comparison against the system linker would establish the exact affected path.

**Still pending:** #489's measured 9700X before/after comparison against #483's record. The current PR description correctly leaves that acceptance item open; a generic 9700X workflow run does not substitute for the specific comparison.

This is a source/contract review, not a locally executed reproduction. I do not recommend treating the as-needed behavior as fully covered until the DSO-reference case is tested.

Re-review of head `9b3329c`:

- **Previous P1 fixed:** `Bind.runtime_needed` now tracks strong unresolved references of selected `-l` DSOs to `libgcc_s.so.1` / the loader, `bind_keep_as_needed` receives the force flag after named-library closure, and `dynamic_inputs` can emit `DT_NEEDED` even without a program-level version import. The new `libhelper.so` integration cases exercise the original reproduction and the own-`DT_NEEDED`, main-definition and weak-reference exceptions. The prior thread can remain resolved.
- **New P2 inline:** The force decision doesn't check whether a different already-needed named DSO brings in the provider through its `DT_NEEDED`. This diverges from GNU ld's `--as-needed` rule and can introduce redundant direct dependencies. A two-DSO test is proposed.
- **9700X CI:** The current commit's 9700X workflow (`40410772915`) completed successfully and ran `test-bind --cross-check`, `test-dynamic --cross-check`, `test-import --cross-check`, the C-driver tests, and the snapshot benchmark. It is a single-head run, **not** the explicitly required paired A/B against #483. That performance evidence is still missing from #489; the PR correctly says `Refs #489` and #515 tracks the writer's split-stack PIE gap.

Source and CI-log review; I did not rerun the compiler locally.

Re-reviewed head `e779132` after the previous P2 comment.

**Prior P2 resolved:** `bind_libraries_loaded()` computes the closure of loaded named DSOs and `bind_runtime_covered()` removes forced `libgcc_s.so.1` / loader dependencies already supplied by their `DT_NEEDED` entries. Both `-lhelper -lplain_needs` orders now have binding and C-driver regression coverage, with GNU ld's `DT_NEEDED` order checked. I found no new actionable correctness defect in this pass.

**CI:** Ryzen 7 9700X run [40422510505](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/actions/runs/40422510505) succeeded. Its logs report 82/82 commands passing, including import, binding, dynamic PIE, snapshot and direct-link tests; c-testsuite is 220/220.

**Acceptance still open (#489):** The job contains standalone measurements for head `e779132`, not the *paired, same-host A/B* comparison with #483 requested by the issue. For context, this head's dynamic snapshot benchmark reports 3,286,696 bytes and `runtime_open` 12.66 µs; #483's published 9700X record reports 3,281,015 bytes and 11.76/11.73 µs. These **cannot be treated as a regression conclusion without a controlled paired run** (host/software and measurement conditions can differ). Please publish side-by-side evidence of snapshot size, `runtime_open`, no-`libgcc_s`-import binding/direct-link latency and the C driver's hello-world runtime, with memory, in buster-performance, before treating #489's performance acceptance as met.

The split-stack dynamic-PIE writer gap remains separately and correctly tracked by #515; the PR correctly uses `Refs #489`, not `Closes #489`.

Source and GitHub CI-log review; I have not executed the compiler independently.

Re-reviewed latest head `01c1343` (six commits beyond my `e779132` review, including the merge of #521 / #515's dynamic-PIE TLS writer).

**New finding (P2, inline):** The writer now rejects an ordinary standalone dynamic-PIE call to `__tls_get_addr`, even with no TLSGD/TLSLD access to relax. This was supported by the previous dynamic-PIE path and differs from normal imported-function linking. `dynamic_test_tls_refusals` currently *expects* the regression. Please preserve non-TLS uses while consuming only verified paired TLS access/call sequences.

**New writer coverage:** Source inspection confirms initial-exec rewriting for imported TLSGD references, local-exec for image-local TLS, and corresponding failure-path checks; the 9700X job [40485437971](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/actions/runs/40485437971) succeeded. Its log reports `unwinder-split-pie` running with 22 relaxed TLS accesses (873 checks, 0 failed), the dedicated TLS fixture passing (280 checks, 0 failed), and 220/220 C tests.

**PR scope/documentation:** The PR description still says split-stack PIEs through Buster's writer are *not* done, are refused at the writer, and belong to #515. That is stale now that #521 was merged into this branch and `dynamic_test_libgcc_s` writes and runs `unwinder-split-pie`, while `test-checker-driver` expects the driver to link it. Update the summary and coordinate #515's status appropriately.

**Performance gate:** I still did not find the specifically requested paired 9700X A/B of this head against #483 in buster-performance (its measurement folders currently contain the #483 baseline and unrelated campaigns). A green single-head CI benchmark is not that acceptance measurement. Keeping `Refs #489` is correct until #489's performance criterion is met.

This is a code/diff and CI-log review; I did not independently execute a reproducer. No merge performed.

Re-reviewed PR #511 at head `8cca727`, compared with my prior review at `01c1343`.

**Previous P2 resolved.** The change scopes consumed `__tls_get_addr` calls to those immediately following TLSGD/TLSLD fixups, excludes only those from the dynamic PIE's GOT/stub accounting, and allows standalone PLT/GOT calls to be patched as ordinary imports. The new `tls-direct-calls` fixture exercises both forms alongside a relaxed TLS access, compares to lld, verifies the emitted variants, and runs with exit status 120. This addresses my previous finding; I found no additional actionable correctness defect in this delta.

**Evidence:** The PR's prior head (`01c1343`) passed the 9700X workflow, including the split-stack PIE and TLS writer tests. The latest head's [9700X workflow](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/actions/runs/40492263502) is *still in progress*, so do not treat its results as passed yet. The PR documents local passes of `test-dynamic --cross-check`, `test-static --cross-check`, `test-executable`, `test-checker-driver`, and `check-call-graph` on `8cca727`; those are author-reported, not independently executed by this reviewer.

**Performance acceptance:** The separate [#515 TLS-relaxation cost record](https://github.com/buster14a/buster-performance/tree/main/docs/measurements/tls-relaxation-515-2026-10-27) is now published (approximately 19 ns per general-dynamic access, 21 ns for imported TLS and 23 ns for local-dynamic in its 180,000-worker synthetic control). However, the *paired* 9700X base-vs-`8cca727` A/B for #489/#511 has not yet been published in buster-performance. The PR's interim `e779132` observations (+0.8 µs runtime_open, +0.05 µs no-GCC-import bind_end and a +0.09 ms / +2.1 MB hello-world result partly attributed to THP layout) warrant the controlled final comparison before signing off the 'no extra cost when unused' criterion. Retaining `Refs #489` / `Refs #515` pending that evidence is appropriate.

No merge performed; source/diff + connected GitHub and existing benchmark-evidence review only.
